ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-intensity white pixels constitute approximately 94% of the visible surface, with low-intensity black pixels accounting for the remaining 6% concentrated along the margins.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: The interior ventral surface is a contiguous solid white field; high-contrast black pigmentation is restricted to a narrow, jagged perimeter along the trailing edge and dense, irregular clusters at the distal lobe tips.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped central depression with a pixel angle of approximately 65 degrees and a moderate depth into the fluke body.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, multi-amplitude serrations present along the entire trailing edge; peak-to-valley variations are most pronounced on the right lobe distal margin with sharp, narrow valleys.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave trailing edges sweep outward from the median notch, transitioning to convex curves at the distal tips of both lobes.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Localized high-contrast dark pixel clusters (circular and irregular) are prominent on the extreme lateral tips of both lobes, suggesting barnacle colonization sites or scarring.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A single short, vertical dark linear disruption is visible on the lower left quadrant of the fluke surface, proximal to the waterline occlusion.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extreme jaggedness and small focal indentations along the trailing edge margins, particularly on the right lobe, indicating significant historical tissue wear.
other_distinctive_markers: Total absence of macro-level mottling or focal pigmentation spots within the central white field of the fluke's ventral surface.
